PANEL_FAMILIES.doc: The panel families of a plugin (omx-panel docs/panel-layout.md): the kind of processor its panel is laid out for. The words and their order are the contract; omx-panel's tools/panel-description.mjs FAMILIES and the skin package schema read them, and keep their code.
PANEL_FAMILIES.why: Panel families and widgets are declarations, so they live here (vocabulary-owner rule, FreeMixer/omx-contract#157).

none.doc: a plugin with no family: its panel is laid out from its groups and roles

text.en: A plugin with no family: its panel is laid out from its groups and its roles.
A gate's or an expander's panel family.
A compressor's panel family.
A limiter's panel family.
A de-esser's panel family.
An equaliser's panel family, parametric or graphic.
A filter's panel family.
A saturator's or a distortion's panel family.

modulation.doc: a chorus, flanger, phaser or tremolo

text.en: A chorus's, a flanger's, a phaser's or a tremolo's panel family.
A delay's panel family.
A reverb's panel family.
A pitch shifter's panel family.

utility.doc: a gain trim, a stereo width control or another utility that shapes a signal without a processor's character

text.en: A utility's panel family: a trim, a width control, a balancer or a clipper.

PANEL_STANDARD_WIDGETS.doc: The standard widgets a panel picks from a descriptor and a representation (a skin) draws, in the order omx-panel's tools/panel-description.mjs STANDARD_WIDGETS lists them.

text.en: A travel, drawn as a knob.
A travel drawn long, as a fader.
A toggle, drawn as a switch.

selector.doc: an integer travel or labelled values

text.en: An integer travel or labelled values, drawn as a selector.
A readout, drawn as a meter.
A response or transfer curve, drawn as a graph.

xy.doc: two controls drawn as one point

text.en: Two controls drawn together as one point on a plane.
A value shown as text.

PANEL_WIDGETS.doc: The widgets a declared panel may name for a control, and the extension serves (org.openmixer.panel-description/1): auto leaves the choice to the panel layout. The four others are the shared widgets of omx-panel's schema/panel.schema.json.

auto.doc: left out of a panel declaration: the layout picks the widget from the control

text.en: Left out of a panel declaration: the layout picks the widget from the control.
A rotary control.
A linear control.
A two-state control.

selector.doc: a control that picks one of a few values

text.en: A control that picks one of a few values.

PANEL_DISPLAY_KINDS.doc: The displays a declared panel may carry, and the extension serves (org.openmixer.panel-description/1), in the order of their codes: a panel description names a display by its place here. omx-panel's tools/panel-description.mjs and omx-clap-core's panel tables read them, and keep their code.
PANEL_DISPLAY_KINDS.why: omx-clap-core restated these words by hand beside the families and widgets; a display kind is a declaration, so it lives here (vocabulary-owner rule).

gainReductionBar.doc: a bar of the gain a dynamics processor takes off

text.en: A bar showing the gain reduction.

transferCurve.doc: a dynamics processor's output level against its input level

text.en: The dynamics transfer curve: output level against input level.
The equaliser's frequency response.
A level meter.

timeResponse.doc: a response over time: a delay's train of taps or a reverb's decay envelope

text.en: The response over time: a delay's taps or a reverb's decay.

PANEL_DISPLAY_SOURCES.doc: Where a panel description's display takes its data from, in the order of their codes (org.openmixer.panel-description/1). omx-panel's tools/panel-description.mjs and omx-clap-core's panel tables read them, and keep their code.
PANEL_DISPLAY_SOURCES.why: omx-clap-core and omx-plugins restated these words by hand beside the families, widgets and display kinds; a display source is a declaration, so it lives here (vocabulary-owner rule).

family.doc: the data the panel family itself implies

text.en: The data the panel family implies.
The plugin's meter readouts.
The gain the processor applies.
A curve the plugin declares.

PANEL_PLACEMENTS.doc: Where an instance sits, in the order of their codes: the clap.track-info/1 flags read as one value (org.openmixer.panel-description/1). omx-panel's tools/panel-description.mjs and omx-clap-core's panel tables read them, and keep their code.
PANEL_PLACEMENTS.why: omx-clap-core and omx-plugins restated these words by hand; a placement is a declaration, so it lives here (vocabulary-owner rule).

insert.doc: an instance on a track's insert chain

text.en: An instance on an insert chain.

return.doc: an instance on a return track

text.en: An instance on a return track.
An instance on a bus.
An instance on the master.

OMX_PARAM_CONTRACT_UNITS.doc: The units of org.openmixer.param-contract/1, the code its get() reports for a parameter's plain value, by token: the LV2 unit a face writes for a descriptor unit (units:db is db), 0..24 the LV2 units one to one, 0x100 and up the vendor block of units LV2 has none for, append-only. A token is served when it has a code here; none is 0.

docs.none: no unit: a plain number, a switch, an index
docs.frame: audio frames (samples) at the running rate
docs.db: decibels, a relative level or a gain
docs.coef: a coefficient, a plain multiplier (1 is unity)
docs.degree: degrees of arc or of phase
docs.dbfs: decibels relative to full scale, 0 the largest sample, a level (vendor block)
docs.dbu: decibels relative to 0.775 V RMS, an analogue level (vendor block)
docs.ratio: a ratio, n to 1, as a compressor states it (vendor block)
docs.lufs: loudness units relative to full scale, ITU-R BS.1770 (vendor block)

STANDARD_SAMPLE_RATES.doc: The standard sample rates (Hz) the desk recognises, the pro-audio superset. One source of truth for the clock controller's `clock.allowed-rates` seed, the force row's validation ceiling and the device-rate probe fallback. What the operator is OFFERED is always the DEVICE's own `supportedRates`; this is the ceiling a write is refused by, never a menu.

STANDARD_QUANTA.doc: The quanta (buffer sizes, in frames, a count with no unit of its own) the console offers: the set a measurement grid or a probe takes its quanta from, beside the rates STANDARD_SAMPLE_RATES lists. A consumer that measures at fewer quanta takes a subset of this list and states it; it never keeps a list of its own. What the operator is OFFERED is still the engine's own choice, this is the ceiling a request is refused by.

RESOURCE_KINDS.doc: Every resource a host plans a plugin for (FreeMixer/plugin-qualify#116): each measured per machine class, judged per host profile, and unknown, never a pass, when it has no figure.

cpu.doc: The cost per sample at a rate and quantum, its percentile and its tail (plugin-qualify#115).

text.en: The cost per sample at a rate and quantum, its percentile and its tail.

memory.doc: The footprint per instance and its growth over a soak (plugin-qualify#114).

text.en: The footprint per instance and its growth over a soak.

scratchMemory.doc: The memory a plugin asks of its host for its process call.

text.en: The memory a plugin asks of its host for its process call.

latency.doc: The frames a plugin delays its output by, per rate and quantum.

text.en: The frames a plugin delays its output by, per rate and quantum.

tail.doc: How long a plugin keeps sounding once its input goes silent.

text.en: How long a plugin keeps sounding once its input goes silent.

voices.doc: The notes an instrument plays at once.

text.en: The notes an instrument plays at once.

startup.doc: The wall time of instantiate, activate and the first block.

text.en: The wall time of instantiate, activate and the first block.

threads.doc: The threads a plugin starts and their scheduling class, or the host thread pool it asks for.

text.en: The block lengths a plugin accepts.

openFiles.doc: The file descriptors a plugin holds after activate, and their growth.

text.en: The bytes a plugin reads at load and while it processes.

state.doc: The size of a plugin's saved state, its save and restore time, and its round trip.

RESOURCE_UNITS.doc: The units a resource figure is given in; an LV2 unit's name where LV2 has one.

text.en: Nanoseconds per sample.
A count of audio frames.
Milliseconds.
Microseconds.
Seconds.
Bytes.
A plain count, with no unit.
A ratio, with no unit.

flag.doc: A yes or a no: one when the plugin does the thing, zero when it does not.

text.en: A yes or a no: one when the plugin does the thing, zero when it does not.

RESOURCE_BASES.doc: How a resource figure was known: what the plugin declares, what a run measured, or a count the caller gave the probe.

text.en: What the plugin declares about itself.
What a run measured.
A count the caller gave the probe.

RESOURCE_HINTS.doc: What a plugin declares about its own footprint, in openmixer's own hints (FreeMixer/plugin-qualify#116): each a claim plugin-qualify measures and checks, carried by the extension below, as the CLAP draft and as LV2 properties. A hint a plugin does not state is unknown, never zero.

footprintAtRest.doc: The memory one instance holds at rest, once activated and idle, with no note playing.

text.en: The memory one instance holds at rest, once activated and idle, with no note playing.

footprintPerVoice.doc: The memory each voice adds while it plays, for an instrument.

text.en: The memory each voice adds while it plays, for an instrument.

sharedLoad.doc: The one-time load every instance of the plugin shares, counted once however many are instantiated.

text.en: The one-time load every instance of the plugin shares, counted once however many are instantiated.

threadsSpawned.doc: The threads the plugin starts itself, apart from any it asks the host pool for.

VERB_HOSTS.doc: The hosts a verb's implementedBy names (docs/contract-dir.md): the programs a controller sends mod-host's protocol to. A verb states what each one owes it; a host the verb leaves out owes it nothing.
VERB_HOSTS.why: A host's verbs were typed twice, in plugin-hostd's protocol.h and in omx-clap-core's command table; a verbs item declares them once, and the hosts it names are a closed list, so a misspelt host is refused rather than read as a host that owes nothing.

pluginHostd.doc: The daemon that places plugins in workers and answers the verbs it adds itself.

PARAM_SCALES.doc: How a host draws a parameter: linear, logarithmic (a frequency, a time) or in discrete steps. The words omx-plugins' declarations and plugin-hostd's protocol use; a travel names its own with `scale`.

PARAM_UNITS.doc: The one list of standard units (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-20, standard vocabulary in one place; docs/units.md): each word's `x-symbol` is its symbol as written (`%`, `""`, `dB/oct`), the word a name the wire can carry, its `x-dimension` what it measures (a word of PARAM_UNIT_DIMENSIONS) and its group its scope (a word of PARAM_UNIT_SCOPES). The schema's $defs.unit enum is the symbols of the `param` units and $defs.descriptorUnit those of the `descriptor` units and `unknown`, in this order (tools/unit-enum.mjs). The list only grows: a unit is appended, never moved or removed. A level's own spellings (an LV2 unit, a CLAP unit code) map onto these ids at that level.
PARAM_UNITS.why: The unit list is declared once (omx-panel docs/behaviour-core.md, decision 3): the panel core and descriptor validation read one list.
